column1: ### Never Hand-Write What an Existing Tool Already Does — 2026-05-28
column2: - **Action**: (a) When an existing tool fails, fix the tool (e.g., add `--yes` flag to `tad.sh`) — don't rewrite it ad-hoc. (b) For new project installation, prefer `*sync` logic (which was just validated on 13 projects) over a one-off script. (c) Post-install verification must include structural comparison: `diff <(ls -d source/.tad/*/) <(ls -d target/.tad/*/)` to catch missing directories. (d) Future improvement: add `tad.sh --non-interactive` or `--yes` flag so it works in Claude Code terminal.

column1: ### Rewiring a Gate's Prose Can Trip a `grep -c` SAFETY Count — Use Line-Set Diff + Re-cite the Constraint - 2026-05-31
column2: - **Action**: For SAFETY/forbidden edits guarded by a substring count: (a) treat the count as a smoke alarm, the line-SET diff as ground truth; (b) classify each "missing" baseline line as forbidden-entry/anchor (must NOT change) vs prose-citation (may be reworded per handoff); (c) when rewording prose that cites a constraint, keep the constraint name in the new text so the count stays stable and the citation accurate; (d) always confirm the anchor with `grep -Fxq` (exact full-line) for byte-identity.

column1: ### A Coverage Gate's Global-Count Floor Cannot Detect Must-Cover SAFETY Loss When Legit Stripping Also Lowers the Count - 2026-06-01
column2: - **Action**: For any gate verifying a preserve-list across an artifact that ALSO legitimately drops items from that list: verify presence per-category within the must-cover scope, never via a global count floor. When designing such a gate, first ask "does the same artifact legitimately remove items I'm counting?" — if yes, a floor is invalid by construction. (Applied: EPIC codex-edition-parity P3 gate AC requires per-SAFETY-category preservation; P2 must trace each must-cover constraint's survival.)

column1: ### Deny-List Beats Allow-List for Sync Sets; Version Grep Must Scope to git-ls-files; diff-r is the Universal Omission Catcher - 2026-06-01
column2: - **Action**: For any growing sync/distribution set: deny-list not allow-list; make the EXCLUSION assertion the load-bearing AC. For version checks: scope to `git ls-files`; prefer false-positive; narrow historical-exclusion to leading-cell. Never pin an absolute count — assert set-equality live. Use `diff -r source==target` as the final "did the copy land completely" verification.

column1: ### Deny-List Must Be Applied at EVERY Copy Granularity, and Verifiers Must Match Each Granularity — 2026-06-01
column2: - **Action**: When converting an allow-list to a deny-list, sweep ALL sibling copy paths at every granularity (dirs, top-level files, nested globs) — fix them symmetrically or the disease relocates. For every copy granularity add a matching verifier granularity. Use `diff -rq source target` (not presence-only) for content-completeness when the source is local. Expose lib internals as FLAGS for any cross-file drift check rather than scraping variable names. Keep self-check fatality comments accurate to the actual `set -e`/trap behavior.
